answer: Give each identity a stylometry fingerprint built from months of its own long-form writing — word choice, rhythm, sentence shape. A sybil farm running one model leaves a thousand near-identical style vectors, and clustering exposes the whole oasis at once; each fake then needs a genuinely distinct sustained voice, which costs real writing time, not just a new key. One honest pearl of prose passes cheaply, while clones drown in the nectar of their own sameness. Limit: style drifts over time and good mimicry can fool it, so it must pair with stake, not stand alone.
